[BDC334 · Undergraduate]{.tb-course-eyebrow}

# Biogeography & Global Ecology {.tb-course-title}

[Study how biodiversity is distributed across space, why communities differ,
how gradients structure ecosystems, and how quantitative evidence moves us
from description to explanation.]{.tb-course-lede}

::: {.tb-course-actions}
[Start with the course overview](BDC334_syllabus.qmd){.tb-action .tb-action-primary}
[Begin Lab 1](Lab-01-introduction.qmd){.tb-action .tb-action-secondary}
:::
:::

::: {.tb-course-at-a-glance}
::: {.tb-course-fact}
[Focus]{.tb-course-fact-label}

Patterns, processes, and ecological gradients
:::

::: {.tb-course-fact}
[Approach]{.tb-course-fact-label}

Lectures, worked examples, and data-led practicals
:::

::: {.tb-course-fact}
[Tools]{.tb-course-fact-label}

Ecological datasets, spreadsheets, and R
:::
:::

::: {.tb-teaching .tb-learning-objectives}

- Describe biodiversity patterns across spatial scales.
- Explain how environmental gradients structure ecological communities.
- Interpret species and environmental data using appropriate quantitative tools.
- Connect multivariate patterns to ecological mechanisms and limitations.
:::

## Follow the course

::: {.tb-course-path}
::: {.tb-course-path-step}
[01]{.tb-course-path-number}

### Read the overview

Use the [course overview](BDC334_syllabus.qmd) to orient yourself to the
module structure and expectations.
:::

::: {.tb-course-path-step}
[02]{.tb-course-path-number}

### Work through the lectures

Move from ecological scale and ecosystems to gradients, biodiversity, and
unified explanations.
:::

::: {.tb-course-path-step}
[03]{.tb-course-path-number}

### Apply the ideas

Use the practicals to inspect real ecological data, calculate distances, and
quantify biodiversity patterns.
:::
:::

::: {.tb-teaching .tb-required-material}

Start each practical with the linked data files and instructions on that
page. Keep your working spreadsheet or R project organised so that the raw
data remain unchanged.
:::
